motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Tooltips and 120-150ms colour transitions on hover.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Closes, tooltip appear, button and link colour changes.

motion.name: duration-medium

motion.name: board-roll

motion.purpose: The departure board's character roll; the one authored moment in the portal. Pausable; skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Springs, staggers, slides, bursts and scenes stop; fades, fills and colour changes that carry state remain; the theme simply switches.

motion.name: intro-arrival
motion.value: GSAP timeline, expo.out; crest parts assemble over about 2.5s, board announcement rolls with ScrambleText

motion.name: intro-glide
motion.purpose: Landing intro hand-over: the platform green narrows onto the sign-in panel and every sign lands on its live counterpart; the board re-rolls to the sign-in values, clipping rather than ellipsing.

motion.name: spring-press
motion.value: linear() sampled from a damped spring (k 520, c 20), 650ms
motion.purpose: Release after a press: back past rest by about a fifth of the press depth.

motion.name: spring-pop
motion.value: linear() sampled from a damped spring (k 400, c 22), 590ms
motion.purpose: Things that land: dialogs, menus, toasts, new rows, roster cells, the stamp.

motion.name: spring-soft
motion.value: linear() sampled from a damped spring (k 300, c 26), 470ms
motion.purpose: Things that slide: the tab pill, the search lens, hover lifts.

motion.name: page-arrival
motion.value: fade 160ms; header and panels rise 14px, 45ms apart, spring k 420 c 32
motion.purpose: How a page inside the portal arrives. Usable from the first frame.

motion.name: theme-sweep
motion.value: view transition, clip-path circle from the pointer, 560ms ease-smooth-out
motion.purpose: A theme chosen from the display menu spreads from where it was chosen.

motion.name: celebration

motion.purpose: Only for a task the visitor just finished, with the stamped toast and the chime.

narrative.overview:
The portal is a station. Bangladesh Railway at Saidpur supplies the whole material: a flag-green rail down the left edge, a board-black departure strip that always says what leaves next, and a platform-white concourse ruled by concrete hairlines. Everything a student reads is either a signboard, a timetable, or a signal. Records (results, receipts, admit cards) leave the station's voice and become paper: official BAUST documents on white, in both themes. The teacher portal is the same station seen from the staff side: the same rail, board and panels, with a section drawn as a roster of numbered cells.

Density is operational, not decorative. Panels sit edge to edge on a 20px gutter, each opened by a condensed capital band and closed by its own hairline, so a laptop screen reads like a timetable page and a phone reads like the same timetable folded into one column. Colour carries meaning before it carries mood: green is the railway and the way forward, amber is "now" and "you are here", maroon is bad news stated plainly. Motion splits the same way the portal does: what a visitor does answers back on a spring (a press gives and returns, a dialog lands, a finished task is stamped and marked with a short burst of tickets), and what a visitor reads stays calm on the house ease-out (records fade in and meters fill, but nothing about a result, a due or a shortfall bounces or celebrates). The board's character roll is the portal's signature moment and the front door has the world's single arrival sequence (see Landing Intro). Under reduced motion every movement stops and the state changes remain.

Light is the daylight platform and the default. Dark is the night-station rendition (deep rail green, near-black ground, mint primary, salmon danger) and keeps every role, including amber, unchanged in meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Flag-green rail and primary actions; board-black strip with amber tabular capitals as the signature.
Archivo on its width axis: condensed capitals for signboards, bands and timetable heads; normal width for UI and reading.
Hairline-ruled white panels on a platform-white ground; shadows only for things that float.
State as signal aspects: green proceed, amber caution or now, maroon danger.
Tabular figures wherever numbers align; currency in the Taka sign.

Playful actions, calm records: springs, bursts and opt-in sounds for what a visitor does; the exponential ease-out for records. The board roll is the portal's signature moment, and the landing intro on "/" is the one authored arrival sequence.

rules.name: The Three Aspects Rule
rules.body: State is shown with exactly three signal colours (ok, caution, danger) plus amber for "now". A new state maps onto one of them; it does not get a new hue.

rules.name: The Amber Is Now Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where it answers "when is it" or "where am I": the board, the current class and the action due for it now (the teacher's roll), the current stop, the active module, your seat, and the burst that marks a task finished this moment. If an amber element answers neither, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Bad News Is Maroon Rule
rules.body: Money owed, failed and referred courses and attendance shortfalls are set in maroon at full size where the student will see them, never softened to grey or buried behind a link.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Condensed capitals are for things a station would paint on a sign: page titles, bands, column heads, the board. Anything a student reads as a sentence is normal width, sentence case. People's names count as sentences: they are never narrowed to fit a box; the box grows, or each name gets its own row.

rules.name: The Columns Align Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a column or can change in place (money, credits, GPA, times, board values, seat numbers) uses tabular lining figures. Only the single headline figure of a panel goes proportional.

rules.name: The Ruled Panel Rule
rules.body: A panel is a white surface with a 1px hairline and a 10px radius. If it has a shadow, it is not a panel; it is floating.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Admit cards, receipts, the exam routine and other official records render as white paper with the float shadow and a 4px radius in both themes, carrying the sample watermark, and print without shadow or radius. A print is always the daylight rendition, whatever the visitor's theme, and every printed document is one page on whatever paper and orientation the print dialog chooses (iOS ignores requested page sizes and adds its own header and footer): a document keeps a fixed design width (44rem, or 66rem for the routines), its height is measured, and the print stylesheet sizes the rem in vw and vh, the page area, so the whole box fits both ways. Tables tighten from 13px rows to 12px past 10 rows and 11px past 18, so long lists stay as large as they can. The routines ask for a landscape sheet where the browser honours it.

rules.name: The Calm Records Rule
rules.body: Springs, bursts and sounds belong to what a visitor does. Records (results, GPA, dues, attendance, referred and backlog courses) only fade in and fill; they never bounce, celebrate or chime.

rules.name: The One Arrival Rule
rules.body: The landing intro is the only authored arrival sequence in the system. No other route may borrow its timeline, its glide or its crest assembly. Pages inside the portal may arrive (see Motion), but only as a quick fade and a capped stagger that never holds back input.

dos: **Do** use flag green for the rail and the one primary action in a view, and keep secondary actions secondary or ghost.
**Do** set page titles in the signboard voice and panel heads in the module band; keep everything readable as a sentence in normal-width sentence case.
**Do** use tabular lining figures for every aligned or live-changing number, and the Taka sign for money.
**Do** separate content with 1px hairlines inside 10px-radius white panels on the platform-white ground.
**Do** map every state onto ok, caution or danger, and use amber only for now and you-are-here.
**Do** state bad news in maroon where the student will see it, with the action to resolve it alongside.
**Do** answer what a visitor does on a spring and mark a finished task with the stamp and a burst sized to it; keep records on the exponential ease-out; stop every movement under reduced motion.
**Do** render official records as white paper with the sample watermark in both themes.
**Do** keep long sheets' save and publish actions in the sticky action bar, with the live count beside them.
donts: **Don't** put a shadow on a panel or a card; shadows belong to floating surfaces and the tab bar only.
**Don't** let motion hold up a task: pages are usable from the first frame, staggers are capped, and no route borrows the landing intro's timeline, glide or crest.
**Don't** introduce a new state colour, or use amber as decoration.
**Don't** set body copy, descriptions or form labels in condensed capitals.
**Don't** soften dues, failed or referred courses, or attendance shortfalls into grey.
**Don't** put springs, bursts or sound on records or bad news, and don't add badges, streaks or emoji; a burst is only for a task the visitor just finished.
**Don't** show photographs of people; avatars are tinted initials.
**Don't** narrow a person's name to fit a cell; widen the cell, or give each student a row.
**Don't** hide, collapse, fade or stage the unofficial-concept plate on the sign-in frame or the landing intro; its only movement is travelling with the intro's glide.
